IT systems are complicated. There are nodes, pods, services, and system resources, sometimes thousands of them, all connected in a complex web of relationships. When things go wrong, it can be difficult to determine the root cause and fix it quickly.

- Slow performance in an application might be caused by heavy load, a memory leak, or a hardware error. Monitoring your infrastructure helps you find the root cause quickly and accurately.
- Running out of disk space can become a disaster for any environment. If you identify the issue early, you can prevent outages.
- When applications or services are co-located, identifying hotspots and conflicts helps you redistribute load correctly.

System downtime can be expensive and disruptive. Observability helps teams detect, triage, and resolve incidents faster.

## Enter observability

Observability is the process of making a system's internal state transparent through the data it produces. It helps you determine whether infrastructure and applications are healthy and functioning normally.

Observability is also a holistic approach. It combines data across all parts of the system so operators, DevOps practitioners, and site reliability engineers can ask new questions when unexpected events happen.
